heroHeadline: Security Cabinet Formally Discusses War Resumption; Haaretz: Netanyahu's Court Filing Is Implicit Oct. 7 Admission — Day 946
heroSubtitle: The deadliest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust — assault timeline, hostage crisis resolved January 2026, intelligence failures, and IDF response. On May 10, 2026 (Day 946 / Ceasefire Day 213), Israel's security cabinet convened its most substantive session yet to formally discuss resuming the Gaza war — with Hamas having rejected every Board of Peace disarmament deadline, and the May 6 Board of Peace declaration releasing Israel from ceasefire constraints. IDF operational plans are reported complete, pending Trump administration authorization; IDF forces were simultaneously destroying a terror tunnel in central Gaza. Haaretz published a landmark May 10 analysis headlined 'Netanyahu Finally Admits What He Spent 31 Months Denying: Oct. 7 Was on Him,' characterizing his High Court filing as an implicit acknowledgment of personal responsibility — contradicting his earlier 'three no's' (no personal accountability, no resignation, no independent commission). Netanyahu's 55-page response to the state comptroller blamed generals and Shin Bet; his simultaneous claim to be 'solely responsible for Israel's security' placed him in a deepening accountability contradiction. 52 days remain until the Supreme Court's July 1, 2026 deadline for the government to present an October 7 investigation framework. Hamas's 1,195-death attack of October 7, 2023 — which triggered 251 hostage-takings (all accounted for as of January 26, 2026) and Operation Swords of Iron — remains the unresolved accountability wound at the heart of Israeli politics. Israel controls 60%+ of Gaza beyond the ceasefire Yellow Line; 850+ Palestinians killed since the October 2025 ceasefire began; 2,400+ ceasefire violations documented.
